name: BattleUnit_Assign
notes: Complete typed implementation behind the BattleUnit_Assign public veneer. It validates the unit and definition IDs, clears the unit record, copies the 84-byte definition's base stats and AI fields, builds the localized display name, expands four ability groups into fifteen slots, initializes equipment, and invokes the unit-stat recalculation owner.

The readable model compiles to 400 bytes against 410 executable reference bytes (412 including alignment). Its broad 69.71 percent structural score claims zero bytes; it is retained as reusable semantic evidence rather than forced through random source shaping.

Independent differential matching locates the same owner uniquely in all six GS1 editions. JA supplies a 378-byte normalized core; EN, DE, ES, FR, and IT each differ in only two core bytes, establishing a narrowly bounded regional compiler/source variant rather than falsely claiming six-ROM identity.

The direct 2,024-byte BattleUnit_Recalculate consumer makes this a coherent 2,436-byte assignment/recalculation family. Existing exact-C item-definition, localized-name, equipment, and ratio-update code supplied the local layout and source-shape analogues.
Recovered only from retained GS1 assembly, exact local GS1 analogues, the approved compiler, and all six local GS1 editions. No GS2 or external source was used.
